metadata.title: Nvidia, CEO Huang sued over disclosures related to suspected Chinese spy

left: On Monday, Nvidia and Chief Executive Jensen Huang were sued in a proposed class action accusing them of defrauding shareholders by concealing Huang's ties with a suspected Chinese spy.

The litigation centers on Huang's alleged affair with Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore-based Megaspeed. The New York Times reported last month that authorities concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset.
Nvidia shares closed down 4.3% on Monday, reducing the company's market capitalization by approximately $190 billion. Such filings follow unexpected share price declines.
Huang told employees he had been unfaithful to his wife, though he did not disclose specific details. The company announced a probe into the matter on Sunday.
Shareholders led by Mark Kistenmacher filed the suit in federal court in San Jose, California, seeking unspecified damages. The document was filed five minutes after market close.
right: Nvidia and CEO Jensen Huang face a proposed shareholder class action alleging they concealed Huang’s ties to Alice Huang, described as a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.
The complaint alleges that Nvidia and Huang misled shareholders about an alleged affair and failed to disclose related national security concerns.
Nvidia announced an investigation into the matter, while its shares fell 4.3%, reducing the company’s market value by about $190 billion.
Shareholders led by Mark Kistenmacher are seeking unspecified damages from Nvidia and Huang.
